record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: To what extent can bias that originates in the data-generating process be detected or mitigated in federated learning, and what methods can apply post-hoc fairness corrections to models learned from potentially biased decentralized interaction data?

evidence.quote: Investigating the degree to which biases in the data-generated process can be identiﬁed or mitigated is a crucial problem for both federated learning research and ML research more broadly. ... Finally, methods for applying post-hoc fairness corrections to models learned from potentially biased training data are also a valuable direction for future work.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a set of clients $\{C_1, \ldots, C_K\}$ each holds a local dataset $D_k = \{(x_{k,i}, y_{k,i})\}_{i=1}^{n_k}$ drawn from a (possibly client-specific) distribution $\mathcal{P}_k$ over an input space $\mathcal{X}$ and label space $\mathcal{Y}$, together with a sensitive attribute $a_{k,i} \in \mathcal{A}$. A global model $f_\theta : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ is trained collaboratively (without centralizing the raw data) by minimizing some federated objective such as $\sum_k \tfrac{n_k}{N} \mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim \mathcal{P}_k}[\ell(f_\theta(x), y)]$. Assume that the data-generating processes $\mathcal{P}_k$ may themselves be biased, in the sense that there exist measurable disparities in conditional distributions across values of the sensitive attribute (e.g., $\mathcal{P}_k(y \mid a = a_0) \neq \mathcal{P}_k(y \mid a = a_1)$) arising from the collection or interaction mechanism rather than from sampling noise.

(a) Develop a rigorous framework, compatible with the federated constraints (clients do not share raw data, communication is limited, and individual data may be subject to privacy mechanisms such as differential privacy), under which one can detect biases that originate in the data-generating processes $\{\mathcal{P}_k\}$. Specifically, give procedures and provable guarantees for identifying when observed disparities in the trained model $f_\theta$ are attributable to bias in $\{\mathcal{P}_k\}$ rather than to optimization, heterogeneity, or finite-sample effects.

(b) Develop federated training algorithms that provably mitigate such data-generation bias under standard fairness criteria (e.g., demographic parity, equalized odds, calibration), with quantitative trade-offs between fairness, accuracy, communication, and privacy.

(c) Develop post-hoc correction methods that, given an already-trained federated model $f_\theta$ and limited (possibly decentralized and privacy-protected) access to client data or summary statistics, produce a corrected predictor $\tilde f$ satisfying a prescribed fairness criterion, with guarantees on the deviation from $f_\theta$ in predictive performance.

Provide methods for (a), (b), and (c), or establish impossibility results delineating the limits of bias detection and mitigation under federated, decentralized interaction-data settings.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad open research direction concerning fairness and bias in federated learning. While numerous partial results have appeared (e.g., fair federated averaging variants, client-fairness reweighting schemes, and post-hoc fairness calibration in centralized settings), no comprehensive solution providing detection, mitigation, and post-hoc correction guarantees specifically for biases originating in decentralized data-generating processes has been established. The problem remains open as a research program.
